title: Raw loop notes — Aya Khan (L4 Runtime Engineer candidate)
content:
Quick raw passback for Aya Khan — impressions while fresh. Notes are messy, intentionally.

Interview context:
- Loop on 2026-03-09 (4 interviews): systems/design, low-latency kernel optimizations, distributed batching, and culture/leadership. Interviewers: Marcus (serving runtime), Evelyn (infra/ops), Priya (team lead, hiring manager), me as recruiter check-in.
- Role: L4 Runtime Engineer (focus: inference performance, KV cache, quantization pipeline). Candidate came via referral (Evelyn).

Immediate gut: strong systems intuition, pragmatic, good tradeoff framing. Not a 10/10 across the board but solid L4 — could be immediate contributor to perf tickets and post-merge guardrails.

What stood out (strengths):
- Very clear on end-to-end latency drivers: network, batching, kernel selection, serialization overhead. Used concrete numbers (p50/p95 examples) which felt credible. Mentioned tailoring kernels by sequence-length distribution rather than model-only heuristics — nice.
- Practical tradeoff sense: when asked about quantization, recommended per-workload accuracy monitoring + canary quantized rollouts instead of universal quantization. Good ops-mindedness.
- Debugging examples: walked through a past incident where a KV cache invalidation bug leaked stale prefixes, and the investigative steps were crisp (log-level toggles, replaying traces, lightweight repro harness). Shows familiarity with production debugging.
- Communicates well with non-specialists — spelled out why a particular optimization mattered for product (e.g., cheaper tokens = cheaper feature).

Concerns / gaps:
- Less depth in large-scale autoscaling policies and multi-tenant fairness. When probed on eviction policies under noisy neighbors, defaulted to simpler heuristics and wanted more data to decide. Not fatal but would need support when we design complex routing policies.
- Limited exposure to HSM/KMS integrations — candidate hasn't owned secure key management for private deployments. Could pair with security engineer initially.
- Some answers were high-level without implementation details: when asked to sketch a batching scheduler that prioritizes latency SLOs, outline looked reasonable but lacked discussion of backpressure and preemption. Again, might be L4 vs L5 question boundary.

Concrete notes from interviews (very short):
- Systems/design (Marcus): liked candidate's sketch for kernel selection cache keyed by (model, seq-dist, hw). Follow-up: asked about staleness and invalidation; answer acceptable but need to document TTL heuristics.
- Kernel optimizations (Evelyn): candidate knows fused attention trends and mentioned memory layout tradeoffs (blocked vs contiguous). Wrote small pseudo-code for tiled matmul — not fully optimized but competent.
- Runtime/ops (Priya): asked about incident postmortems and runbooks. Candidate has runbook authorship experience for 2 incidents, suggested integrating eval prompts into alerting pipeline.
- Culture: good collaborator, admits knowledge limits, asks clarifying Qs; seemed mindful about mentorship.

Scorecard (my quick pass):
- Technical (runtime & perf): 4/5
- Production experience & debugging: 4/5
- Scaling / infra policies: 3/5
- Leadership / communication: 4/5
- Overall recommendation: strong hire for L4; recommend onsite/culture debrief and one follow-up on autoscaling design (short take-home or 30-min follow-up with SRE).

Suggested follow-ups / interview tweaks if we progress:
- Add a short, focused question on multi-tenant throttling/fairness and preemption in the loop (30m). We need to ensure they can reason about noisy-neighbor mitigation beyond heuristics.
- Optional: brief take-home to design a canary rollout for quantized models that includes metrics and rollback triggers (keeps eval focus).

Notes for hiring packet:
- Highlight practical incident debugging examples + runbooks.
- Mention limited KMS/HSM ownership; flag for pairing with security during ramp.
- Include suggested mentoring plan first 3 months: pair with Evelyn on kernel land and with SRE on autoscaling policies.

Open questions I want answered before final:
- Does she have direct experience with on-prem private control plane installs? She implied limited operator-run experiences. Confirm.
- Can she write a small batching scheduler prototype in python within a day? If we ask take-home, keep it lightweight.

Random small quotes to include in write-up: "I prefer canaries + realtime evals over wholesale quantization, because you can catch regressions early" — good soundbite.

Action items (my suggestions):
- Move to hiring packet + short follow-up on autoscaling/policy (30m with SRE).
- If follow-up goes well, proceed to reference check and comp discussion.

Draft snippet for passback doc (one-liner):
- Aya shows strong runtime engineering chops, pragmatic tradeoff thinking, and solid production debugging experience. Recommend progressing with a targeted follow-up on autoscaling & multi-tenant fairness before final decision.

Other small TODOs for me:
- Add JIRA-INF-4321 as linked artifact and attach interview recordings.
- Send quick TL;DR to Priya and Marcus with this passback and ask for any counterpoints within 48h.

End of scratch — keep short/casual in packet. Will refine after follow-up.
